messages.subject: limma analysis
parts:
Hi everyone,

I've got some questions about limma analysis with aroma.affymetrix (or with data generated by aroma.affymetrix).

Since there is no detailed information about FIRMA available so far (Are there any status-updates?), I would like to do a 't-test-like' test on the exon-level-estimates. The general outline would be as follows. The data is four HuEx-1_0-st-v2-chips per group (treatment/control). The chips are unpaired. So I could do a t-test for every exon (I would expect to do this on "core"-exons) and get around 18708 p-values (t-statistics). Then I could plot a histogram with 20 columns on the x-axis: column1 0<=p<0.05, column2 0.05<=p<0.10 and so on. If there is no difference between control and treatment I would see equally distributed data at a level of 18708/20 \approx 935. So any data in column1 above this level would suggest that there is something alternativly expressed. The amount of exons in column1 above the 'by-chance threshold' would give me a vague idea whether there is some alternative expression in my data (and I should invest more time for further analysis) or not. I also thought of volcano plots which could could give me exons with a low p-value and high log-fold change.

So far for the general idea. For several reasons a limma test seems to be appropriate for this. I know the limma package is well documented but as I understand it, some of you are quit familiar with this package and since there is so much to do wrong, I would appreciate some help very much.

Suppose I have done (the usual) BG-Adjustment, Normalization and Summarization already.
...
> plmEx <- ExonRmaPlm(celsetN, mergeGroups=FALSE)
> fit(plmEx, verbose=verbose)
...
How do I continue from here? As far as I understand it, the essential step in the limma analysis is
> fit <- lmFit(eset,design)
> fit.eBayes <- eBayes(fit)

How do I "convert/export" the CelSet 'plmEx' from affymetrix.aroma to the 'eset' for limma? How do I setup the design model?

Could someone help me out with some lines of code or so? Or at least point out the relevant section in the limma user manual? Or maybe if you have objections concerning the whole approach let me know too.

Thanks a lot (again),
Frank

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] limma analysis
parts:
Hi Frank,

So I just finished some changes to the FIRMA paper which was holding me
back from putting it online, so I should be able to put it up soon.

In terms of the analysis you are suggesting, the main problem (if I
understand you correctly) is that you would just look for differences in
exon expression between the two groups. This will not pick up just
alternative splicing but also any differential expression at the gene
level (i.e. common to all exons within the gene). A better route, if you
want to go this way, is to take the affymetrix approach calculate what
they call the 'splicing index' -- the difference between the gene and
exon expression -- and look for group differences there. The SI will not
be zero centered and also will depend on the gene specific noise, so is
not itself easy to compare across genes. However, if you are doing a
t-test this would iron itself out.

To do this
plmGene <- ExonRmaPlm(celsetN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
fit(plmGene, verbose=verbose)

plmEx <- ExonRmaPlm(celsetN, mergeGroups=FALSE)
fit(plmEx, verbose=verbose)

exDF<-extractDataFrame(plmEx,addNames=TRUE)
exDF[,-c(1:5)]<-log2(exDF[,-c(1:5)]) #the first 5 columns are the names
geneDF<-extractDataFrame(plmGene,addNames=TRUE)
geneDF[,-c(1:5)]<-log2(geneDF[,-c(1:5)])

In prinicipal, you could then calculate the SI by subtracting from each
exon expression (row) of exDF from the appropriate gene (row) expression
in geneDF. However, you have to line up which exons go with which genes.
By choosing 'addNames=T', you will have the 'unitName' (the gene
identifier) in both dataframes so you can match them up (DON'T use other
output, such as 'unit', 'group' or 'groupName' since these will not line
up between the two data frames). I have simple code below (i.e. slow)
that does this given the dataframe imputs (on the log scale). Then you'd
just take that dataframe and create the necessary input (I think limma
will take just matrix too, it's quite nice and flexible). If you went
the FIRMA route, you could also do extractDataFrame on the firma object
and do comparisons (or even limma analysis) on that data frame.

Now I'm assuming you're only using 'core' exons, etc. These data frames
will not be unmanagable in this case (the exon around 300,000 rows and
the gene around 20,000 rows) -- I can do this on my laptop.

Note, that you might also want to filter based on the exDF. It will
actually be in the same order as the firmaDF you would get out from the
FIRMA analysis too, so the same filter could be used for either analysis.

Best,
Elizabeth

calculateSI<-function(geneEffectsDF,exonEffectsDF,skip=1:5){
units<-geneEffectsDF$unitName
if(any(ncol(geneEffectsDF[,-skip])!=ncol(exonEffectsDF[,-skip])))
stop("Matrices do not match")
SIDF<-exonEffectsDF
SIDF[,-skip]<-NA
cumMatch<-NULL
for(i in 1:length(units)){
whMatch<-which(exonEffectsDF$unitName==units[i])
cumMatch<-c(cumMatch,whMatch)
if(length(whMatch)==0){
warning("Unit",i,"is not found in the exon data frame")
next;
}
geneEff<-as.numeric(geneEffectsDF[i,-skip])

SIDF[whMatch,-skip]<-sweep(data.matrix(exonEffectsDF[whMatch,-skip]),2,geneEff,"-")

}
if(length(cumMatch)!=nrow(exonEffectsDF)) warning("Some units in
exon data frame were not found in the gene data frame")
return(SIDF)

}

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: limma analysis
parts:
Hi all.

Just thought I'd interject with a couple thoughts on this, given that I
had suggested limma previously.

If I understand your question, you are looking for differentially
expressed transcripts OR differentially spliced transcripts between your
two groups (Ctrl/Normal).

Personally, I don't like running limma or any statistical test for
differential expression (DE) at the exon (PSR) level. The reason is
twofold: i) you pay a huge price in multiple testing (think ~200000
tests), and ii) if an exon is DE, you don't know whether it is actually
the gene that is DE or if it is differentially spliced (DS).

My feeling is you'd want to do a two-step approach: first, look at
gene-level DE (mergeGroups=TRUE fitting), then look at differential
splicing (i.e. FIRMA scores). So, you could run limma on your gene-level
expression estimates to look for DE and you could run limma on the FIRMA
scores to look for DS (Note: you have to pay the multiple testing price
here).

A gene can be differentially expressed as well as differentially spliced
(and its not clear that we can always disentangle the two), but at least
these two steps give you an indication of it.

Either way, its always helpful to look at the probe-level data for the
genes/exons that come out as significant.

Hope that is helpful.

Mark

Hi,

I tried the code Elizabeth posted above and want to give some feedback.

First of all one small remark: extractDataFrame is a method of ParameterCelSet and so the correct code has to be:

...
> plmEx <- ExonRmaPlm(celsetN, mergeGroups=FALSE)
> fit(plmEx, verbose=verbose)

> cesEx <- getChipEffectSet(plmEx)  # newline here !!!
> exDF <- extractDataFrame(cesEx,addNames=TRUE) # changes here!!!
...

Everything else works fine -- thanks a lot. But I think your function rather should be called "calculateNI" because whats basically done there is to calculate the log of the "gene-level normalized intensity" (see attachment "NI-SI.jpg" of the Affy Tech Report). I extended the function in a pretty quick and dirty way and now it calculates the SI between the (in my case two) groups and does an unpaired, two-sample t-test for every PSR. With (a very small subset of) this data I made a volcano plot, which looks pretty convincing (see attachment "volcano_simplescatter.png"). Could maybe someone run over the code at the end and have a look if I did somthing completely wrong?

Another thing, that I'm still not completely certain about is the unit-group-cell thing. I think, this strongly depends on the used cdf. So lets assume I did not use the Affy-cdf but instead HuEx-1_0-st-v2,controlR3,A20071112,EP.cdf. So then the units would be transcript clusters/genes, right? And the goups would correspond to the PSRs/Exons, right? And the number of groups per unit would be an indirect measure of the number of annotation sources, right? For "core" this should be mostly more than 1... But what is "cell" than?

Another problem is, how can get "real" names for my transcript clusters? With "real names" I mean a name that I can query at www.ensembl.org for instance. Do I have to use "HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl49,G-Affy.cdf"? Suppose I want to know the name of the transcript cluster with name "2315251" in HuEx-1_0-st-v2,controlR3,A20071112,EP.cdf. Can I look up this unitname in HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl49,G-Affy.cdf or will I get mixed up? Although the U-Ensembl49-cdf has more units it is not guaranteed, that every unit from the controlR3-cdf is also in the U-Ensembl49-cdf, right?  <-- I'm a bit confused...

Frank

######
calculateSI<-function(geneEffectDF,exonEffectDF,skip=1:5,group1, group2){
    units<-geneEffectDF$unitName
    if(any(ncol(geneEffectDF[,-skip])!=ncol(exonEffectDF[,-skip])))
stop("Matrices do not match")

SIDF<-exonEffectDF
    SIDF[,-skip] <- NA
    SIDF[,"p.value"] <- NA
    SIDF[,"t.stat"] <- NA
    SIDF[,"SI"] <- NA
    skip <- c(skip,max(group2)+1,max(group2)+2,max(group2)+3) #cols for p.value, t.stat. and SI were added

cumMatch<-NULL
    for(i in 1:length(units)){
whMatch<-which(exonEffectDF$unitName==units[i])

cumMatch<-c(cumMatch,whMatch)
      if(length(whMatch)==0){
            warning("Unit",i,"is not found in the exon data frame")
            next;
            }

geneEff<-as.numeric(geneEffectDF[i,-skip])
        SIDF[whMatch,-c(skip,max(group2)+1,max(group2)+2,max(group2)+3)]<-sweep(data.matrix(exonEffectDF[whMatch,-skip]),2,geneEff,"-",check.margin=TRUE)
      for (j in whMatch){
            SIDF[j,"p.value"]    <- t.test(SIDF[j,group1],SIDF[j,group2])$p.value
            SIDF[j,"t.stat"]    <- t.test(SIDF[j,group1],SIDF[j,group2])$statistic
            SIDF[j,"SI"]        <- mean(as.numeric(SIDF[j,group1]))-mean(as.numeric(SIDF[j,group2]))
        }
    }
    if(length(cumMatch)!=nrow(exonEffectDF))

warning("Some units in exon data frame were not found in the gene data frame")
    return(SIDF)
}

Sorry, about that. You are correct, extractDataFrame needs to be on a
ChipEffectSet.

> Another thing, that I'm still not completely certain about is the
> unit-group-cell thing. I think, this strongly depends on the used cdf.
> So lets assume I did not use the Affy-cdf but instead
> HuEx-1_0-st-v2,controlR3,A20071112,EP.cdf. So then the units would be

unit,group, and cell are ALL cdf dependent; moreover, for the output of
the ChipEffectSet when mergeGroups=T there is only 1 value per unit and
it's stored arbitrarily under the first group slot, so it gets a group
identification which is nonsensical (which is why I said use the
'unitName' to match things). For mergeGroups=F, however, the
group/groupName identifies the probeset. For cdf distributed by Affy,
the unit and group are identical (except for some controls) and there is
no grouping of exons/PSRs into genes/TC. In my cdfs (e.g.
HuEx-1_0-st-v2,coreR3,A20071112,EP.cdf) they have been grouped and unit
refers to TrCluster. (I'm not sure why you are using 'controlR3' in all
your questions, which is only control probes, rather than 'coreR3' --
you shouldn't use controlR3 for an analysis of AS)

And the goups would correspond to the
> PSRs/Exons, right? And the number of groups per unit would be an
> indirect measure of the number of annotation sources, right? For "core"
> this should be mostly more than 1... But what is "cell" than?

I don't understand this question: for the coreR3 cdf (or any cdf
grouping the exons) the number of groups per unit is merely the number
of PSRs per transcript cluster. Which is more or less the number of
exons per gene (really there are more PSRs than exons). In the Affy cdf,
it's mostly 1 group per cdf. I don't understand how the number of
annotation sources comes in...

Cell basically refers to an actual spot on the array (an indexing value
for each element of data that could be stored in the corresponding CEL
file).

>
> Another problem is, how can get "real" names for my transcript clusters?
> With "real names" I mean a name that I can query at www.ensembl.org
> <http://www.ensembl.org> for instance. Do I have to use

> "HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl49,G-Affy.cdf"? Suppose I want to know the name
> of the transcript cluster with name "2315251" in
> HuEx-1_0-st-v2,controlR3,A20071112,EP.cdf. Can I look up this unitname
> in HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl49,G-Affy.cdf or will I get mixed up?
> Although the U-Ensembl49-cdf has more units it is not guaranteed, that
> every unit from the controlR3-cdf is also in the U-Ensembl49-cdf,
> right? <-- I'm a bit confused...
>

The unit names in 'coreR3' type cdfs are the transcript clusters. the
unit names in U-Ensembl*,G-Affy cdfs have units corresponding to ensembl
ids (but the groups are according the Affy PSR, which is what the G-Affy
means). So the group names in the two are both the PSR names, so they
are the same, but there is no (simple) relationship between the unit
names. There is annotation of Affy that relates TC to genes (though
sometimes TC involves more than 1 gene), but I don't know whether genome
browsers can look up the names of TC. I tend to use the Ensembl cdf
because I can quickly look up the names (with biomaRt) and plot with
GenomeGraphs the results. Also, genes with significant overlap were
concatenated into one unit, but otherwise overlapping probes were thrown
out in the Ensembl cdf, unlike the TC definitions.

Elizabeth

> In terms of the analysis you are suggesting, the main problem (if I
> understand you correctly) is that you would just look for differences in
> exon expression between the two groups. This will not pick up just
> alternative splicing but also any differential expression at the gene
> level (i.e. common to all exons within the gene). A better route, if you
> want to go this way, is to take the affymetrix approach calculate what
> they call the 'splicing index' -- the difference between the gene and
> exon expression -- and look for group differences there. The SI will not
> be zero centered and also will depend on the gene specific noise, so is
> not itself easy to compare across genes. However, if you are doing a
> t-test this would iron itself out.
>
> To do this
> plmGene <- ExonRmaPlm(celsetN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
> fit(plmGene, verbose=verbose)
> plmEx <- ExonRmaPlm(celsetN, mergeGroups=FALSE)
> fit(plmEx, verbose=verbose)
> exDF<-extractDataFrame(plmEx,addNames=TRUE)
> exDF[,-c(1:5)]<-log2(exDF[,-c(1:5)]) #the first 5 columns are the names
> geneDF<-extractDataFrame(plmGene,addNames=TRUE)
> geneDF[,-c(1:5)]<-log2(geneDF[,-c(1:5)])
>
> In prinicipal, you could then calculate the SI by subtracting from each
> exon expression (row) of exDF from the appropriate gene (row) expression
> in geneDF. However, you have to line up which exons go with which genes.
> By choosing 'addNames=T', you will have the 'unitName' (the gene
> identifier) in both dataframes so you can match them up (DON'T use other
> output, such as 'unit', 'group' or 'groupName' since these will not line
> up between the two data frames). I have simple code below (i.e. slow)
> that does this given the dataframe imputs (on the log scale). Then you'd
> just take that dataframe and create the necessary input (I think limma
> will take just matrix too, it's quite nice and flexible). If you went
> the FIRMA route, you could also do extractDataFrame on the firma object
> and do comparisons (or even limma analysis) on that data frame.
>
> Now I'm assuming you're only using 'core' exons, etc. These data frames
> will not be unmanagable in this case (the exon around 300,000 rows and
> the gene around 20,000 rows) -- I can do this on my laptop.
>
> Note, that you might also want to filter based on the exDF. It will
> actually be in the same order as the firmaDF you would get out from the
> FIRMA analysis too, so the same filter could be used for either
